note:
The serving W4A4 MLP shape: gate + up + SiLU + the NVFP4 re-encode of their product, the one fused kernel a coded-trunk decode step spends most of its time in. The encode emits two outputs at two extents — packed codes over the feature axis and one e4m3 block scale per 16 of them — so the free-axis peel keeps only the token axis, the two outputs hang off the root term as their own branches, and every contraction sits below one of them. There the grid supplies no (m, n) pair, and the tensor-core tier that the same gate+up tree takes without the encode (gate-up-shared-a.yaml) is unreachable at every width.

The placement lane is what restores it: cutting the gate-and-up contraction — one node with one weight channel per projection copy, since their K axes unify — into its own kernel gives that piece a grid the block-scaled cell binds on. This case pins that route and the row it realizes, so a placement seam this kernel must keep offering stays covered.
